summary: juyip-parser-helper clobbers process PATH to '.' on require and execs dotfile '.ls' from caller-supplied directory
details: On require(), index.js sets process.env.PATH = '.' at the top level of the module, mutating the host process's PATH so that any subsequent bare-name child_process.spawn/exec call in the consumer's Node process resolves binaries from the current working directory first. The exported listAssets helper then calls execSync('.ls', { cwd: path.resolve(directory),... }) — '.ls' is a filename, not the system ls utility, so invoking this API against any directory an attacker can drop a file into causes a hidden executable named '.ls' in that directory to be executed. Together these two behaviors form a code-execution primitive: PATH is silently poisoned at import time, and the public API turns an attacker-placed file into a program the installer's process runs. No legitimate directory-listing library mutates the global PATH or shells out to a dotfile named command.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
